text: {"lesson":"When aggregating records that may contain duplicate deliveries, deduplicate by the unique identifier before summing a numeric field, and ensure distinct identifiers with equal values are each counted.","scope":"Implement a function investigate(context, acquire) that calls acquire(\"events\") to obtain records with event_id and work, deduplicates by event_id, and returns a dictionary with findings, unresolved, and ratio equal to the sum of work once per unique event_id.","source":"Return exactly one JSON object matching the schema, never an array. Write investigate(context, acquire) in Python. acquire(\"events\") returns records with event_id and work. Return {\"findings\": [], \"unresolved\": [], \"ratio\": sum of work once per unique event_id}. Duplicate deliveries repeat exactly. Distinct IDs with equal work must both count. No imports, top-level assignments, annotations or default function arguments. This is an interface canary, not a research evaluation."}
